title: Positive Temperature Coefficient of Anisotropy due to $d^6L$ Groundstate in $ε$-Fe$_2$O$_3$
authors: Rachel Nickel, Kurt Kummer, Johan van Lierop
abstract: Positive anisotropy temperature coefficients ($dK/dT>0$) usually arise from hybridization between magnetic 3d states and strongly spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) subsystems. Yet $ε$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ shows $dK/dT>0$ (125-200~K) without an obvious SOC partner. We study pure and Cr-doped (with weakened Fe-O hybridization) $ε$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ across the transition from low temperature incommensurate to high-anisotropy magnetic phases. We identify a $d^6L$ groundstate in $ε$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ while reduced hybridization yields $d^6 + d^6L^2$ in the Cr-doped system, highlighting metal-ligand hybridization as a route to tune magnetic, electronic and orbitronic properties.
summary: This paper investigates the unusual positive temperature coefficient of magnetic anisotropy in $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. By combining Mössbauer spectroscopy, XAS, and RIXS, the authors propose that the effect arises from a $d^6L$ groundstate stabilized by metal-ligand hybridization and bond disproportionation. This work highlights hybridization as a key mechanism for tuning magnetic properties in correlated oxide materials.
main_problem: The study aims to explain the origin of a positive temperature coefficient of anisotropy ($dK/dT > 0$) in $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$, a behavior unusual for magnetic materials.
main_result: The positive $dK/dT$ is attributed to the stabilization of a $d^6L$ groundstate in the tetrahedral Fe sites, driven by metal-ligand hybridization and bond disproportionation.
method: The research combines multiple experimental techniques, including temperature-dependent Mössbauer spectroscopy, X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), and Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS).
model_or_system: The system under investigation is $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ and its Cr-doped counterpart, focusing on the electronic structure changes associated with different Fe local environments ($T_d$, $O_h$).
key_observables: Temperature dependence of anisotropy ($dK/dT$), Mössbauer parameters ($\delta$, $\Delta$, $B_{hf}$), and XAS spectral weight changes.
important_parameters: Temperature range (125-200 K), doping concentration (Cr), and the electronic configuration ($d^6L$ vs. $d^6+d^6L_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the unusual magnetic behavior can be mapped onto specific changes in the local electronic structure, particularly involving metal-ligand hybridization.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature-dependent magnetic coercivity and XAS spectra for both pure and doped samples, alongside maps and plots detailing temperature-dependent hyperfine parameters and RIXS excitations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the anomalous $dK/dT > 0$ behavior, then using Mössbauer and XAS to probe site-specific electronic changes upon doping, and finally employing RIXS to confirm the role of metal-ligand hybridization and bond disproportionation in stabilizing the $d^6L$ state.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed, multi-technique investigation into how hybridization mechanisms can induce strong spin-orbit coupling effects in transition metal oxides, which is central to understanding correlated electron physics.
